item.title: Transferability of classical uncoupled ductile-damage criteria to fracture prediction in single-point incremental forming over a controlled geometrical process window
item.description: 库内相似论文：Numerical prediction of failure in single point incremental forming using a phenomenological ductile fracture criterion（相似度 0.813） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：Micromechanically-motivated phenomenological Hosford–Coulomb model for predicting ductile fracture initiation at low stress triaxialities [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijsolstr.2015.02.024] 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 与《Lode dependent plasticity coupled with nonlinear damage accumulation for ductile fracture of aluminium alloy》共享 9 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.137 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1617732343, https://openalex.org/W2016102352, https://openalex.org/W2032768430, https://openalex.org/W2035518577, https://openalex.org/W2048598423 延性断裂准则: 可作为断裂轨迹形式与起裂判据的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定试样组合、是否覆盖你的应力状态区间、有无独立验证试样 摘要片段: The Modified Mohr–Coulomb, Cockcroft–Latham, and Johnson–Cook … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: Johnson-Cook, Mohr-Coulomb 比较评估线索；改进扩展线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 摘要方法线索: Mohr-Coulomb 改进扩展线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Transferability+of+classical+uncoupled+ductile-damage+criteria+to+fracture+prediction+in+s&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmatprotec.2026.119532%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22ductile_fracture%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Uncoupled ductile damage criteria applied to processes involving non-proportional and non-monotonic loading, such as single-point incremental forming (SPIF), are commonly calibrated using standard characterization tests conducted under proportional monotonic loading. Prediction discrepancies may reflect incomplete coverage of the calibration domain or limitations of the criterion formulation. This study examines both explanations, evaluating transferability at three levels: discrimination between fractured and non-fractured configurations, preservation of their relative experimental ordering, and fracture localization. A process window for AA5754-H111, defined by wall angle and in-plane shape, comprised nine configurations spanning the transition from non-fractured to consistently fractured conditions. The Modified Mohr–Coulomb, Cockcroft–Latham, and Johnson–Cook criteria were assessed by comparing the experimental fracture results with predictions obtained from finite-element simulations validated against surface strain fields measured by digital image correlation. All three criteria predicted fracture-threshold crossing in every configuration, including non-fractured ones, and did not preserve the complete experimental ordering. Their damage maxima nevertheless lay within the fractured region in two of the three consistently fractured cases and approximately 15 mm from the crack in the third, compared with 30 mm for the equivalent-plastic-strain maximum. Nonlinear accumulation restored neither discrimination nor ordering, whereas mapping the calibrated loci as fracture forming limit curves better distinguished fractured and non-fractured configurations in principal-strain space. A joint calibration of the Modified Mohr–Coulomb criterion combining the characterization tests with fractured SPIF cases still produced mean absolute percentage errors in equivalent plastic strain at fracture of 46.1% for the characterization tests and 31.0% for the SPIF cases, indicating that adding process data did not resolve the conflict within this functional form. The conflict therefore cannot be attributed to calibration coverage alone. Process data can establish whether a common calibration exists, but their inclusion alone cannot reconcile the criterion formulation with both characterization and process histories. Abstract Dual-phase Mg–Li alloys display interesting mechanical properties, including an unusual increase in ductility at low strain rates due to grain refinement. The effects of grain size, testing temperature and strain rate on the flow stress of an Mg-8wt.% Li alloy processed by high-pressure torsion were investigated through mechanical tests at low strain rates and through machine learning algorithms trained on data in the literature. The data are also compared to the deformation mechanism of grain boundary sliding. The experimental results and creep analyses show a high strain rate sensitivity and ductility and a low activation energy in the material, suggesting the dominance of thermal activated deformation mechanisms. The mechanism of grain boundary sliding is able to predict the trends revealed by experiments, while machine learning models suggest the temperature as the most significant parameter in flow stress. The ability of the black-box and white-box machine learning algorithms to make predictions and errors of models is discussed. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+In-situ+resistance+heating-ultrasonic+vibration+composite+forming+of+TC4+alloy+sheet%3A+Expe&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmatprotec.2026.119533%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 To improve the manufacturing efficiency and dimensional accuracy of aerospace TC4 alloy sheet components, an in-situ resistance heating and ultrasonic vibration-assisted V-bending (RHUAV) composite forming process was developed. Increasing vibration amplitude enhances acoustic softening and reduces forming force and springback, whereas increasing ultrasonic frequency weakens these effects because of ultrasonic energy attenuation. More importantly, a thermo-ultrasonic microstructure-regulation mechanism is revealed, linking phase transformation, grain rotation, and dislocation redistribution to improved deformation coordination. This coupled regulation promotes dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement during RHUAV forming. Based on these mechanisms, a dislocation-density-based unified constitutive model and a process parameter–forming effect mapping model were established to predict dislocation evolution, flow behavior, forming force, and springback, with prediction errors below 4%. Engineering validation was performed using the base plate of an aero-engine flow path plate. Compared with conventional isothermal forming, RHUAV reduced the short- and long-side springback ratios by 63.3% and 77.8%, increased impact toughness by 19.3%, and improved manufacturing efficiency by 80.2%, while also refining the microstructure and improving surface quality. These results demonstrate that RHUAV provides an efficient route for integrated shape–property control of aerospace titanium alloy sheet components. item.title: Role of post-necking softening in the ductile failure of pure titanium
item.description: 库内相似论文：Evaluating the ductile failure characteristics of CuZn30 brass under different stress conditions（相似度 0.739） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 引用重点论文：Lode dependent plasticity coupled with nonlinear damage accumulation for ductile fracture of aluminium alloy [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matdes.2017.09.064] 与《Plasticity, ductile fracture and ballistic impact behavior of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy》共享 7 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.165 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W2032768430, https://openalex.org/W2047055714, https://openalex.org/W2048598423, https://openalex.org/W2761900377, https://openalex.org/W2967627908 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: The study systematically investigates ductile failure … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 塑性变形与硬化律: 可作为硬化律选型与颈缩后外推方案的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定应变范围、外推是否有独立验证、是否混用不同试样 摘要片段: Commercially pure titanium grade 2 exhibits … Commercially pure titanium grade 2 exhibits a distinct deformation profile: a short strain hardening stage followed by prolonged post-necking ductility, behavior inadequately captured by conventional hardening laws. To address this, a modified coupled plasticity–damage model is proposed to accurately reproduce the stress–strain response of the material. The study systematically investigates ductile failure under variable stress triaxialities and Lode angles using five distinct specimen geometries: dog-bone, notched, two in-plane shear configurations, and hat-shaped compression. A fully coupled ductile damage–plasticity model, explicitly accounting for stress triaxiality and Lode angle, is implemented alongside a non-linear damage evolution law. Three modified Ganjiani, KHPS, and DF2016 failure criteria are studied due to their comparable predictive accuracy. Experimental data are validated through ABAQUS/Explicit simulations using VUSDFLD and VUHARD, demonstrating good agreement in force evolution and fracture strain across all geometries. Digital image correlation further confirms the fidelity of the simulations. The initiation of failure is geometry dependent: for dog-bone and notched specimens, it coincides with the onset of slope reduction post-plateau; for shear, shear-tension, and hat-shaped compression specimens, failure initiates at the onset of hardening, where the slope of the force–displacement curve begins to decrease significantly. These findings provide a robust framework for predicting ductile failure in the material studied under complex loading. item.category: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

Ductile fracture in metallic materials involves substantial plastic deformation, shear localization, damage accumulation, and eventual crack propagation—phenomena that pose significant computational challenges when combined. We present an arbitrary-order virtual element method (VEM) for ductile fracture using a fourth-order phase-field formulation coupled with rate-dependent plasticity. The fourth-order phase-field regularization provides sharper crack representation and improved accuracy compared to standard second-order models, but requires 𝐶 1 -continuous elements that complicate numerical implementation. We address this challenge by employing 𝐻 2 -conforming VEM for the fourth-order phase-field equation and 𝐻 1 -conforming VEM for the momentum balance equation. The plastic response is modeled using the Bodner–Partom viscoplastic constitutive model with a plastic degradation function that couples damage evolution to plastic deformation. Numerical examples demonstrate the capability to simulate complex ductile fracture phenomena including shear band formation, crack nucleation from plastically deformed regions, and dynamic crack propagation. The results demonstrate this framework as a powerful computational tool for modeling ductile fracture processes using polygonal elements. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+symbolic+regression-corrected+Arrhenius+constitutive+model+for+high-temperature+deformat&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.09.178%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 During high-temperature plastic deformation, material flow stress is jointly affected by deformation temperature, strain rate, and strain. Its accurate prediction is essential for hot-working process optimization and finite element simulation. To address the limitations associated with the predefined functional form and residual prediction errors of the strain-compensated Arrhenius constitutive model, a symbolic-regression-corrected strain-compensated Arrhenius model based on deep symbolic optimization, termed SR-ARH, was developed using hot-compression data for ECO-AlMag8, Haynes 230, Cu-Sn alloy, and TC4. The framework employs an RNN-guided, GP-assisted strategy to identify explicit correction-factor expressions. The operator set was constrained according to the nonperiodic and nonlinear characteristics of high-temperature flow-stress evolution. Based on feature-importance analysis, SR-ARH-2F was developed using temperature and strain rate, followed by SR-ARH-3F with strain as an additional feature. The SR-ARH-3F model exhibited superior overall predictive performance compared with the SR-ARH-2F model and was therefore selected as the final model. Leave-one-condition-out validation revealed condition-dependent generalization performance under unseen deformation conditions, while strain-hardening-rate analysis showed no obvious nonphysical oscillations within the calibrated range. Compared with the strain-compensated Arrhenius model, the SR-ARH-3F model reduced RMSE by 3.397-15.574 MPa and AARE by 3.428-8.177 percentage points, while increasing R by 0.00616-0.04747. Hot-compression simulations were further performed using DEFORM-2D. The load-displacement curves obtained from simulations using the SR-ARH-3F model showed closer agreement with the experimental curves, and the corresponding load AARE was reduced by 0.188-19.099 percentage points relative to simulations using the strain-compensated Arrhenius model, confirming the applicability of the proposed model to numerical simulations of hot compression. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Process-referred+ductile+damage+parameter+identification+approaches+for+modelling+crack+pr&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.cirpj.2026.09.011%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22calibration%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The innovative process chain for steel fiber production based on sheet metal by notch rolling and fulling shows great potential, but requires further analysis of the process steps’ interactions for fundamental process understanding and design. Given their high variability, the analysis based on simulations offers a viable approach, requiring a sufficient damage model to predict material failure of notched sheet metal under cyclic bending load. Material parameters of damage models are often determined inversely based on characterization tests, ignoring their physical meaning. After further calibration, no pure material- but process-dependent parameters result. In addition to the conventional approach, considering the Lemaitre and GISSMO damage models, the study at hand introduces an alternative inverse parameter identification of the Lemaitre damage parameters based on the process itself, accepting that no pure material parameters and no broadly applicable model are retained. Both methods for parameter identification, conventional and process-referred, are applied for cyclic bending of stamped DP600 wire strip. The evaluation based on the comparison of simulative and experimental torque courses during cyclic bending shows that the Lemaitre model determined by the process itself reaches good agreement due to comparable stress state of high triaxiality. The conventionally determined GISSMO damage model and the Lemaitre model determined by tensile test show significant deviations. The agreement of the conventionally determined Lemaitre model could be improved by considering a notch tensile test as reference during inverse identification, causing a different state of stress triaxiality, but still process-referred method proved more effective by requiring less experimental effort for target-oriented modeling in engineering applications. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+Numerical+Study+on+the+High-Velocity+Ballistic+Performance+of+TPMS+Sandwich+Structures&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.48084%2Fetasr.18947%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%2C+%22impact_validation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structures have significant potential for lightweight ballistic armor. Unlike previous quasi-static or low-velocity studies, this research explicitly addresses the terminal ballistic regime and perforation morphology. It evaluates three Ti6Al4V TPMS sandwich cores (Diamond, Gyroid, Primitive) subjected to 7.62 mm Armor-Piercing (AP) projectiles at 830 m/s using Abaqus/Explicit. By coupling a tuned shell-based full-scale architecture approach with Johnson-Cook damage evolution, severe element-distortion instabilities were successfully eliminated. The Diamond topology exhibited the most efficient ballistic efficiency, achieving an optimal Specific Energy Absorption (SEA) of 118.27 J/g at a 10% relative density. This structural tuning yielded a 94.3% core mass reduction compared to monolithic RHA steel of equivalent dimensions while mitigating 95% of the initial kinetic energy. Furthermore, the tortuous curvature of the Diamond and Gyroid architectures forced a highly localized failure zone, preventing the catastrophic macroscopic fracture observed in the Primitive topology. These findings establish a robust framework for designing scalable, weight-optimized TPMS ballistic shields for next-generation combat vehicles and aerospace applications. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Strain+rate+effect+on+frictional+behaviour+of+Hardox+450+steel&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1007%2Fs00170-026-19262-4%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract The influence of strain rate on the frictional behaviour of high-strength Hardox 450 steel have been investigated using both experimental and numerical approaches. The ring compression test method was employed to identify the friction coefficient across a wide range of strain rates, from quasi-static (0.005 s -1 ) to dynamic conditions (3 000 s -1 ) utilizing a split Hopkinson pressure bar test. Tests were conducted under dry conditions and with MoS 2 grease lubrication. The results demonstrate a significant decrease in the friction coefficient with increasing strain rate; for dry friction, the value dropped from 0.176 to 0.015. It was observed that at high strain rates (1 000 s -1 ), the friction coefficients for both dry and lubricated conditions converge, suggesting that the lubricant’s effect becomes negligible and the strain rate itself becomes the dominant factor. The material’s flow stress was characterized using the calibrated Johnson-Cook constitutive model. Based on the experimental data, a new explicit mathematical function describing the nonlinear dependence of friction on strain rate was proposed. This model was subsequently verified via finite element method simulations, showing high agreement between the predicted and experimental shapes of the deformed rings. Hot stamping of 22MnB5 boron steel enables high-strength automotive components, but local deformation and damage may develop in geometrically constrained regions such as the sidewall–bottom-corner transition. A thermo-mechanically coupled DEFORM-3D finite element model was developed to examine local temperature, effective stress, effective plastic strain, and Damage under variations in die-entry temperature, punch speed, and friction coefficient. The deformation-sensitive region remained spatially stable, though its response magnitude varied with process conditions. Increasing die-entry temperature (750–850) °C reduced effective stress through thermal softening, with little change in final effective plastic strain and Damage. Increasing punch speed (50–150) mm×s-1 improved temperature retention and reduced effective stress, but increased effective plastic strain and Damage; increasing friction coefficient (0.3–0.7) substantially increased effective plastic strain and Damage with only limited effects on temperature and stress. Final Damage correlated strongly with final effective plastic strain ( R 2 = 0.99, partly reflecting the cumulative NCL formulation) but showed a weaker correlation with final effective stress ( R 2 = 0.62), indicating that instantaneous stress and accumulated Damage may exhibit different process-dependent trends and should therefore be considered jointly when assessing local deformation and damage accumulation. Abstract In this study, the effects of post-aging conditions on the mechanical properties, deformation behavior, and fracture characteristics of 6082-T6 aluminum alloy sheets were investigated, using tensile testing supported by Digital Image Correlation (DIC). Post-aging treatments were performed at 100, 200, 300, and 400 °C, with holding times of 30, 60, and 90 minutes at each temperature. The following parameters were determined from the tensile tests: yield strength, tensile strength, strain-hardening exponent, uniform elongation, total elongation, and energy absorption capacity. Microstructural and fracture analyses were performed using optical microscopy (OM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while X-ray diffraction (XRD) was used to evaluate phase-related structural changes. Hardness variations were assessed by Vickers hardness testing (HV5). Fracture-surface dimple morphologies were quantitatively evaluated using average dimple diameter and standard deviation values to assess the temperature- and time-dependent variation in fracture behavior. The results showed that aging at 200 °C for 60 min provided a highly favorable strength–ductility balance and was identified as the most efficient processing condition in terms of the combined mechanical response, with a yield strength of approximately 289 MPa, tensile strength of about 400 MPa, uniform elongation of 15.9%, total elongation of 17.4%, hardness of 115.6 HV, and energy absorption of 61.36 MJ/m³. At 300–400 °C, pronounced overaging occurred as precipitate coarsening reduced the effectiveness of precipitation strengthening, leading to significant degradation in mechanical performance. The strain-hardening response and energy absorption capacity were found to be strongly dependent on the aging condition. The results indicate a transition from relatively homogeneous deformation to strain-localized behavior as aging temperature increases, consistent with reduced deformation stability at elevated temperatures. Overall, these findings demonstrate that controlled post-aging can tailor the strength–ductility balance and fracture response of AA6082-T6 sheets. Glazing used in security, defence, transport, and critical infrastructure must provide clear visibility while offering reliable protection against ballistic threats. Conventional float glass is attractive for its optical clarity and compressive strength. However, it is also inherently brittle that leads to sudden cracking, fragmentation and rear face spalling when subjected to high velocity impact. As a result, float glass is unable to withstand handgun ballistic loading. Laminated glass which comprising multiple glass plies bonded by polymeric interlayers has become a solution. In this research a simulation model was developed in LS-DYNA R13 to evaluate the ballistic performance of two laminated glazing configurations: a triple laminated glass with polyurethane (PU) interlayer (S1) and a double laminated glass with PU interlayer clad polycarbonate at the back (S2). Soda lime glass layers were represented using the Johnson–Holmquist ceramic model (MAT_110) to capture brittle fracture, while polycarbonate and PU interlayers were modelled using MAT_24 to simulate strain rate plasticity. 9 mm Luger full metal jacket (FMJ) projectile was defined using the Johnson–Cook plasticity model, and the boundary conditions, impact velocity, and shot spacing were matched to the experimental setup. The simulations reproduced key failure mechanisms observed in experiments, including cracking, fragmentation, and rear face spalling. The simulation results show that the double laminated glass with PU interlayer clad polycarbonate at the back (S2) successfully stopped the projectile with residual velocity of 0 m/s, exhibit localized polycarbonate bulging that absorbed and dispersed impact energy as compared to a triple laminated glass with polyurethane (PU) interlayer (S1) which have experienced complete perforation. The evolutionary trajectory of accelerated testing techniques for high-temperature materials is systematically reviewed in this paper—from classical accelerated factor approaches centered on the Arrhenius model and the inverse power law model, to time-temperature parameter methods represented by the Larson-Miller parameter, further to physics-based accelerated models incorporating damage mechanics, and finally to new intelligent accelerated testing paradigms exemplified by “directed truncation” and the “unified damage mechanics-based acceleration equation.” On this basis, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) are further introduced as a key bridge linking physical models and data-driven methods, and their core roles are elucidated in damage state inversion, small-sample parameter identification, and load-life mapping modeling. A holistic conceptual framework, termed “Mechanism-Data-Performance Integrated Accelerated Validation” (MDPI-AV), is proposed. Its core functionality is realized through the synergy of multi-scale mechanism modeling, multi-source data fusion, PINN-driven parameter identification, and intelligent test design, thereby establishing a credible “fidelity mapping” between high-dimensional accelerated stresses and long-term service damage mechanisms. The key innovation of this framework is identified as the “mechanism-consistency-guaranteed adaptive directed truncation” method—by which damage mechanisms are recognized in real time through multi-modal in-situ monitoring, the truncation criterion is defined by a mechanism consistency index, and the test process is dynamically optimized via Bayesian updating. Furthermore, a “unified damage mechanics-based acceleration equation” is proposed, which integrates the Lemaitre-Chaboche nonlinear continuum damage mechanics with the Strain Range Partitioning (SRP) concept. By this equation, creep, fatigue, oxidation, and multi-field coupling effects are unified within a single internal variable evolution framework, thus fundamentally solving the quantification challenge of multi-physical field synergistic effects. The MDPI-AV framework is considered to represent a paradigm shift in accelerated testing technology from “blind acceleration” to “precise inquiry.” A systematic solution is thereby provided for the credible validation of the 100,000-hour-plus long-life performance of hot-section components in gas turbines. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Beyond+Composition%3A+A+Geometry-Aware+Framework+for+Functionally+Graded+Material+Design+Dem&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1007%2Fs11661-026-08385-8%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract Functionally graded material (FGM) design has typically focused on designing compositional paths between terminal alloys to avoid cracking. In this study, a framework is developed to vary both composition and geometry for desired spatial- or component-level properties. To efficiently characterize mechanical properties for FGM component design, a multi-material property characterization process was developed to extract multiple compositions’ constitutive behavior simultaneously from variable-width FGM tensile specimens. The mechanical performance of Monel 400-Inconel 625 (IN625) FGM tensile specimen was used as a representative example to demonstrate the geometry and composition FGM design framework. Published: 2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Metallurgical and Materials Transactions A 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考 重点作者新作: Allison M. Beese

item.title: Analytical model to characterize temperature-dependent anisotropic-asymmetric behavior of Mg-Gd-Y alloy
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Modeling of temperature- and stress state-dependent yield and fracture behaviors for mg-gd-Y alloy（相似度 0.769） 被相关论文引用：Ductile fracture model across wide stress state considering void evolution [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engfracmech.2026.112654] 与《A lode-dependent plasticity model for high-strength structural steel》共享 4 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.088 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1969052431, https://openalex.org/W2757592523, https://openalex.org/W3046100037, https://openalex.org/W4294630901 温度效应与热软化: 可作为温度项形式、软化机制与绝热升温修正的建模参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对温度区间、加热方式、是否等温、绝热升温是否已修正 摘要片段: Thermal softening effect is not significant … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 塑性变形与硬化律: 可作为硬化律选型与颈缩后外推方案的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定应变范围、外推是否有独立验证、是否混用不同试样 摘要片段: • https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Analytical+model+to+characterize+temperature-dependent+anisotropic-asymmetric+behavior+of+&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jma.2024.11.035%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 • Uncovering temperature-, loading direction- and stress state-dependent plastic behavior of a Mg-Gd-Y alloy. • Developing a combined swift-voce model with the temperature variable to describe the temperature-dependent plastic behavior. • Characterizing the evolving temperature-dependent anisotropic-asymmetric yield behavior with the plastic strain. • Capturing the three-point bending deformation behavior under various temperatures by the proposed A-Yoon2014+SVT model. The work is conducted to uncover and simulate the dependence of the evolving anisotropic-asymmetric yield behavior on the temperature for an Mg-Gd-Y alloy. Experiments were carried out at 25∼300 °C, including uniaxial tension and compression. The strength is observed to decrease non-linearly as the temperature increases. Thermal softening effect is not significant when the temperature is lower than 200 °C, but the strength decreases dramatically at high temperature than 250 °C. Tension-compression asymmetry and anisotropy are observed to be strongly and nonlinearly dependent on strain and temperature. The temperature effect is taken into account in a combined Swift-Voce (SVT) model to predict the temperature-dependent strain hardening behavior with a higher accuracy than the traditional Johnson-Cook and Zerilli-Armstrong equations. An analytical Yoon2014 (A-Yoon2014) yield function is established to capture the evolving anisotropic-asymmetric behavior with respect to strain and temperature. The predicted force-stroke curves of the A-Yoon2014+SVT model are closer to the experimental results of the three-point bending process than the numerical results of the original Yoon2014+SVT model. Given its user-friendliness and high accuracy for the modeling of temperature-dependent anisotropic-asymmetric hardening behavior, the A-Yoon2014+SVT model is recommended to be utilized in the numerical simulation of plastic forming process for hexagonal close-packed metals. Published: 2024-12-19T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Journal of Magnesium and Alloys 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考 重点作者新作: Yanshan Lou
